title: Homework 4 (Electronic) — Amplifier Analysis and Design Reasoning
preamble: Type your answers directly in this app. Every part on this assignment is answered on screen; nothing is printed, photographed, or scanned. Show your reasoning in words as well as numbers — the AI-graded parts are read for the argument, not just the final value.

problems.name: Common-Emitter Stage
problems.description: A common-emitter amplifier is biased at I_C = 1 mA with R_C = 4.7 kOhm, driven from a source with R_S = 600 Ohm. Assume beta = 150 and V_T = 26 mV at room temperature.

subsections.name: Is the stage inverting?
subsections.description: State whether this stage inverts the signal, and justify your answer in one or two sentences by reference to the direction of collector current change.

subsections.name: Small-signal voltage gain
subsections.description: Compute g_m and the small-signal voltage gain A_v = -g_m * R_C. Give the numeric result and state the assumption you made about the output loading.

subsections.name: Effect of source resistance
subsections.description: Explain how the 600 Ohm source resistance changes the gain you would actually measure at the output, and identify which element of the small-signal model is responsible.

problems.name: Design Trade-offs
problems.description: You are asked to raise the gain of the stage in Problem 1 without changing the supply voltage.

subsections.name: Propose and defend a design change
subsections.description: Propose one change to the circuit that raises the voltage gain, work through its effect on bias point, headroom, and bandwidth, and explain what you are giving up. A complete answer names the trade-off explicitly rather than only describing the benefit.

subsections.name: Final numeric answer
subsections.description: State the new voltage gain produced by your proposed change, as a single number with units.

subsections.name: Annotated schematic
subsections.description: Upload a photograph or export of your revised schematic with the changed element marked.
